proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–107), second assertion (test functions approximating the indicator of the cone {|x| ≤ 2|⟨x, normal⟩|} ∩ B_1(0) show that its density vanishes), applied to μ. This is parent proof Steps 1 and 3 with all details filled in; the plane ball B_{θ(1+1/α)}(0) is open, exactly as in the parent, so the sibling plane_ball_measure (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_ftd_plane_ball_measure) applies directly, and the sibling test_upper_bound supplies the eventual radius restriction that the parent expresses as "0 < r ≤ r₀/2".

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, P := (span{v})^⊥, H^m := μHE[m], ν := H^m⌞P, I(g) := ∫_P g dH^m = ∫ g dν, I_r(g) := r^{-m} ∫ g(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z), and S_r := {z : α‖z − y‖ ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_r(y). Fix r₀ > 0 with μ(B̄_{r₀}(y)) < ∞ and fix α > 0.

0. Preliminaries. v ≠ 0, so finrank P = m (orthogonal complement of a line in the (m+1)-dimensional E; Submodule.finrank_orthogonal_span_singleton). P is a finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace, so it is Borel measurable. ω_m = unitBallVolume m is the Lebesgue measure of a bounded set, so ω_m < ∞; put ω := toReal(ω_m) ≥ 0, so ω_m = ofReal(ω). By the sibling plane_ball_measure (N := m + 1, the same m, Q := P), for every s > 0: ν(B_s(0)) = H^m(B_s(0) ∩ P) = H^m(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_m · ofReal(s^m) = ofReal(ω s^m) < ∞; so 1_{B_s(0)} is ν-integrable with ∫ 1_{B_s(0)} dν = ω s^m.

1. The set K := {w : α‖w‖ ≤ |⟨w, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_1(0) is nonempty (0 ∈ K); it is closed and bounded (hence compact), though only nonemptiness and K ⊆ B̄_1(0) are used below.

2. Fix θ > 0 and define g(w) := max(0, 1 − dist(w, K)/θ). Then: g is continuous, since w ↦ dist(w, K) is 1-Lipschitz; 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, since dist ≥ 0; g = 1 on K, since dist(w, K) = 0 for w ∈ K. If g(w) ≠ 0 then dist(w, K) < θ (otherwise 1 − dist(w, K)/θ ≤ 0 and g(w) = 0), so, K being nonempty, there is k ∈ K with ‖w − k‖ < θ.

3. Compact support. If g(w) ≠ 0, take k as in 2; then ‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − k‖ + ‖k‖ < θ + 1. So g vanishes outside the compact ball B̄_{1+θ}(0) and has compact support.

4. Behaviour on P. Let ρ := θ(1 + α^{-1}) > 0. Claim: if w ∈ P and ‖w‖ ≥ ρ then g(w) = 0. Suppose instead g(w) ≠ 0 and take k ∈ K with ‖w − k‖ < θ. Since w ∈ P, ⟨w, v⟩ = 0, so ⟨k, v⟩ = ⟨k − w, v⟩. Since k ∈ K, Cauchy–Schwarz and ‖v‖ = 1 give α‖k‖ ≤ |⟨k, v⟩| = |⟨k − w, v⟩| ≤ ‖k − w‖‖v‖ = ‖w − k‖ < θ. Thus ‖k‖ < θ/α, and ‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − k‖ + ‖k‖ < θ + θ/α = ρ, contradicting ‖w‖ ≥ ρ.

5. Plane integral. I(g) ≤ ω ρ^m: by 4 and g ≤ 1, g ≤ 1_{B_ρ(0)} at every point of P, hence ν-almost everywhere (ν is the restriction of H^m to the measurable set P). Since g ≥ 0 and 1_{B_ρ(0)} is ν-integrable, monotonicity of the integral gives I(g) ≤ ∫ 1_{B_ρ(0)} dν = ω ρ^m by step 0.

6. Apply the sibling test_upper_bound (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_ftd_test_upper_bound) with N := m + 1, the same m, μ, y, f := g, A := K, L := I(g), L' := ωρ^m + θ and the given r₀. Its hypotheses hold: g is continuous, compactly supported (3) and ≥ 0; g ≥ 1 on K (2); I_r(g) → I(g) by the hypothesis; and I(g) ≤ ωρ^m < ωρ^m + θ by 5 and θ > 0. It gives: eventually μ({z : r^{-1}(z − y) ∈ K}) ≤ ofReal((ωρ^m + θ) r^m).

7. Inclusion. For r > 0, S_r ⊆ {z : r^{-1}(z − y) ∈ K}: if z ∈ S_r and w := r^{-1}(z − y), then α‖w‖ = r^{-1}(α‖z − y‖) ≤ r^{-1}|⟨z − y, v⟩| = |⟨w, v⟩| (as r^{-1} > 0), and ‖w‖ = r^{-1}‖z − y‖ ≤ 1 since ‖z − y‖ ≤ r. With 6 (and the eventual set {r > 0}), for every θ > 0, eventually μ(S_r) ≤ ofReal((ω(θ(1 + α^{-1}))^m + θ) r^m).

8. Conclusion. In [0, ∞], X_r → 0 iff for each ε > 0, eventually X_r ≤ ε. If ε = ∞ this is trivial. Otherwise t := toReal(ε) > 0. The function φ(θ) := ω(θ(1 + α^{-1}))^m + θ is continuous on ℝ with φ(0) = ω · 0^m + 0 = 0 because m ≥ 1 (this is the only use of m ≥ 1). Hence there is θ > 0 with φ(θ) < t. By 7, eventually r > 0 and μ(S_r) ≤ ofReal(φ(θ) r^m) ≤ ofReal(t r^m) = ofReal(t) · ofReal(r^m) = ε · ofReal(r^m), so μ(S_r)/ofReal(r^m) ≤ ε. Therefore μ(S_r)/ofReal(r^m) → 0 as r ↓ 0, for every α > 0. ∎
